newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -- Stg seen vulnerable below 2.44 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -- Stg seen vulnerable below 2.44 marks.

text.p: Sterling/mark suffered its largest setback in months on Monday and a break below 2.44 could quickly unwind some of its hard-won gains since the summer, technical analysts said.
The pound hit a 22-month high at 2.4568 marks on Friday but the price action did not coincide with a higher relative strength index (RSI), suggesting a retreat may be in store.

"A break below 2.44 marks automatically targets 2.43 and adds fuel to the fire," said Darren Spain, currency analyst at Credit Suisse. "We had the largest pullback in the whole rally and it coincides with daily bearish divergence on the RSI."
Sterling has risen with few interruptions since August 2, when it set a daily low of 2.3736 marks.
But the afterburners really kicked in on October 11 when sterling/mark broke above 2.4035, leaving large price gaps on charts.
"It is such a steep trend that it overshot the top of a bull channel and it is probably due to come back a little at this point," said Scott Siller, senior techincal analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
On Monday the pound peaked at 2.4560, failing to set a higher daily high for the first time since October 8.
Some analysts are concerned that a break below Monday's subsequent low at 2.4405 could result in an even steeper correction as the market looks to fill pricing holes left on the way up.

"If it gives way, it gets pretty bleak to about 2.4036 marks," said David Durrant, senior currency strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc. "Because it moved up quickly on the other side there is a little bit of a hole in the business."
At 1600 EDT on Monday, sterling/mark was trading at 2.4430/40.
